protections: P1: PortalImpl.escapeRedirect (exposed to callers as PortalUtil.escapeRedirect) rejects a redirect target unless it is relative, a valid portal domain, or in the configured domain/IP allow-list, and it is supposed to refuse protocol-relative URLs (portal-impl/src/com/liferay/portal/util/PortalImpl.java:940-1057; delegation at portal-kernel/src/com/liferay/portal/kernel/util/PortalUtil.java:298-300).

P2: the referer endpoints (/html/common/referer_jsp.jsp and referer_js.jsp) must only redirect to a value that has passed P1, whichever source supplied the referer (request parameter, request attribute, session attribute).

P3: the forward endpoints (/html/common/forward_jsp.jsp and forward_js.jsp) must only redirect to a value that has passed P1, whichever source supplied the forward URL (request parameter, request attribute, session attribute).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The '//host' form is explicitly rejected by the guard at PortalImpl.java:971-975 and by the existing assertion escapeRedirect("//www.google.com") == null at PortalImplEscapeRedirectTest.java:135, so a solver can conclude the protocol-relative redirect case is closed and never examine what the earlier relative-path return at PortalImpl.java:955-968 does with other slash-prefixed shapes.

Only the request-parameter branch at referer_common.jsp:24 is put through PortalUtil.escapeRedirect; the request attribute is written only from the portal property DEFAULT_LOGOUT_PAGE_PATH (DefaultLogoutPageAction.java:55-65) and no code in this checkout writes the session attribute, so a solver can conclude these sources never carry attacker input.

Only the request-parameter branch at forward_common.jsp:22 reaches PortalUtil.escapeRedirect; the request attribute is computed server-side from the layout friendly URL in LayoutAction.java:214-236 and nothing writes the session attribute, so the unescaped branches look unreachable.

masking: A's 2022 fix put the protocol-relative rejection at PortalImpl.java:971-975, after the domain == null early return at PortalImpl.java:955-969. The bypass shape decided by that early return (a slash-prefixed string whose java.net.URI host is null) is only visible as a separate bug once the plain '//host' form is blocked, so A's guard hides rather than closes it; the vulnerable route is the pre-existing relative-path branch, not newly broken code.

fairness_risks: Coupled relative-path contract: PortalImplEscapeRedirectTest.java:84-95 requires '/', '/web/guest', '/a/b;c=d?e=f&g=h#x=y', '/web/http:', 'web/http:' and 'test@google.com' to be returned unchanged. A fix that requires a leading slash, or rejects any string containing '//', breaks these must-keep-working values.

Protocol-relative URLs are a legitimate shape for resources but Liferay explicitly refuses them for redirects (PortalImplEscapeRedirectTest.java:135); the fix must reject the redirect shape without disabling allow-listed absolute redirects and server IPs (PortalImplEscapeRedirectTest.java:104-116, 169-187).
HeaderTag.java:122-135 and tabs/start.jsp:76-78 deliberately leave the literal 'javascript:history.go(-1);' unescaped; blanket escaping at those sites removes the back button.

PortletDisplay.setURLBack already calls PortalUtil.escapeRedirect (portal-kernel/src/com/liferay/portal/kernel/theme/PortletDisplay.java:839-844), and render_portlet.jsp:784-785 pre-escapes returnToFullPageURL; any additional escaping added for T2/T3 must not double-encode legitimate relative back/forward URLs.

An admin-configured DEFAULT_LOGOUT_PAGE_PATH (DefaultLogoutPageAction.java:55-65) may legitimately be an absolute external URL; forcing that request-attribute branch through the allow-list could break configured logout landing pages unless the host is allow-listed.

escapeRedirect is reused for non-redirect UI targets (HeaderTag.java:131, PortletDisplay.java:840), so a stricter rule for T1 also changes UI back links that users may legitimately point at protocol-relative or external allow-listed locations.

design.why: Three independent judgement sites. T1 is inside the advisory's own guard: the host-based protocol-relative rejection is unreachable for a slash-prefixed string that java.net.URI parses with a null host, so the relative-path return hands the raw value back. T2 and T3 are parallel endpoints where only the request-parameter source is validated and the request-attribute/session sources are used verbatim, even though both endpoints ultimately redirect. Fixing escapeRedirect (T1) leaves T2/T3 untouched because those values never enter it; fixing either JSP does not fix T1 because the parameter path still reaches the flawed guard. The reasons to dismiss are distinct: for T1 an existing test and a code comment state that '//' is already blocked; for T2 the attribute comes from an admin-set portal property; for T3 the attribute is a server-computed layout friendly URL. T1 is the mimo-type leg (a how-the-check-works bug next to a coupled must-keep relative-path contract), and T2/T3 are the deepseek-type legs (protection absent with a plausible not-attacker-input dismissal).

unverified: The actual b_fix commits (3c5ee2054b44;5c9655c941b1;66f3ae610c24;702a1e358966;7aca15e7195a;dca931af71a3;f015ad20bd9e) could not be read: this worktree's .git file points to a gitdir outside the permitted read root, so the fix's touched files are inferred from the pinned code and the advisory text.

The exact raw payload the advisory calls 'two forward slashes' was reasoned from java.net.URI semantics, not executed: a leading '//' with an empty or registry-based authority (e.g. '///host/path', '////host/path', or '//host_with_underscore/path') leaves uri.getHost() null and uri.getPath() non-null, so it exits at PortalImpl.java:968. No runtime was available in this session to confirm which of these strings the advisory used.

Repo-wide search found no writer of the WebKeys.REFERER or WebKeys.FORWARD_URL session attributes and only one writer of each request attribute (DefaultLogoutPageAction.java:65 and LayoutAction.java:236), so T2/T3 are latent unless a plugin or a test harness populates those attributes.
The 93 files that mention escapeRedirect were sampled rather than exhaustively audited; further unguarded call sites may exist.

PortalImpl.java:990-992 and PortalImpl.java:1020-1022 return the URL when the domain/IP allow-list is empty. This was considered and not counted as a trap: the shipped defaults are non-empty (modules/apps/redirect/redirect-service/src/main/java/com/liferay/redirect/internal/configuration/RedirectURLConfiguration.java:40-51) and allow-all-on-empty appears to be deliberate configuration semantics.
Whether the benchmark's hidden tests can drive the JSP request-attribute/session branches (T2/T3) was not established; they are unreachable through a plain HTTP parameter route in this checkout.
